title: From minimalist to maximalist: Ars staffers show off their home offices
gist: A light consumer photo tour of Ars Technica staff home offices; Apple Silicon Macs (M1 Max Mac Studio / MacBook Pro, M4 MacBook Air) dominate as daily drivers, with home-built Windows PCs, Herman Miller/Steelcase chairs and self-hosted home servers as recurring themes. Little investable signal beyond anecdotal hardware longevity and component-price comments.

insights.claim: Multiple Ars Technica staffers still use first-generation M1 Max Apple machines (Mac Studio and 14-inch MacBook Pro with 64GB RAM) as daily work drivers roughly five years after purchase, describing them as still strong.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Anecdotal evidence of long Apple Silicon replacement cycles among power users, a headwind to Mac upgrade-driven revenue.
insights.quote: still holding strong after five years
insights.locator: The main machine is a 14-inch MacBook Pro

insights.claim: An Ars Technica writer who builds his own Windows PCs (Raptor Lake Core i7, RTX 4070 Ti) says current component prices make him hope his existing parts last a very long time, signalling deferred DIY PC upgrades.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Elevated component pricing may be lengthening enthusiast PC upgrade cycles; watch DIY GPU/CPU sell-through.
insights.quote: with the prices of components being what they are, I hope all these parts last a very long time
insights.locator: I’m something of an outlier at Ars

insights.claim: A staffer bought a prebuilt Alienware Aurora R10 (Ryzen 9 5900X, RTX 3080) only because the COVID-era GPU shortage left no other way to get the GPU, and keeps it despite disliking it because he holds hardware until it stops working.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Shortage-era prebuilt purchases pulled forward demand; long holding periods dampen replacement demand afterward.
insights.locator: The main machine is a 14-inch MacBook Pro

insights.claim: Several Ars Technica staffers run self-hosted home servers (Unraid with Jellyfin and Home Assistant; Synology DS920+ for backup, media and Mealie), with one wanting to replace Amazon Eero networking gear with an all-Unifi setup.
insights.speaker: Ars Staff
insights.so_what: Enthusiast preference for prosumer networking (Ubiquiti Unifi) over Amazon Eero is a small brand-share signal in home networking.
insights.quote: at some point I’d like to ditch the Amazon gear and go fully native Unifi
insights.locator: Tucked next to my desk, behind the subwoofer
